suggestions.moderator: Individualized-coaching dose (cycles or coaching-contact hours per year)
suggestions.definition: Among PD models that include coaching/mentoring, the realized intensity of the one-to-one component: number of coaching cycles per teacher per year, or coaching-contact hours per week/month. Candidate levels (continuous, or binned): high (~weekly / >=10 cycles/yr) / moderate (biweekly-to-monthly / 5-9 cycles) / low (every ~6 weeks or fewer). Distinct from total TPD hours (already coded) and from the binary coaching principle: it is the dose of the individualized feedback channel specifically.
suggestions.rationale: Allen explicitly halved coaching intensity for scalability (5-6 cycles/yr vs 10-12 in the original MTP-S efficacy trial) and still got g=0.48, while Babinski's lighter coaching (on-site only every ~6 weeks) returned mostly nulls and Bierman/Abe's near-weekly on-site mentoring (~3 hrs/classroom/wk) produced the strongest emergent-literacy effects. If coaching is the active ingredient, its per-teacher dose - not aggregate program hours - is the lever, and these papers vary it widely and discuss it as causal.

suggestions.moderator: Independence of the evaluation from the program developer
suggestions.definition: Whether the study's authors/evaluators have a financial or proprietary stake in the program being tested. Levels: developer-conducted / developer-affiliated authors (co-own or distribute the program) / independent third-party evaluation (e.g., government REL/IES contractor with no stake). Distinct from the already-coded 'trainer = researcher/developer vs external', which is about who delivers the PD, not who runs and reports the trial.
suggestions.rationale: Classic source of effect inflation. In this batch the positive headline effects come from developer-linked teams (Allen & Ansari: R. Pianta co-owns the MTP dissemination company; Borman: several SFA co-authors are Success-for-All-Foundation-affiliated, study hosted on the developer's site), whereas the independent REL/IES evaluations (Abe REL Pacific, Arens REL Central) return small or null confirmatory effects. Independence plausibly moderates measured g and is reportable from author affiliations/COI statements.

suggestions.moderator: Follow-up lag between end of PD and outcome measurement (in years)
suggestions.definition: Elapsed time from the end of the teacher's PD/student-facing intervention to the achievement measurement, as a continuous lag. Levels: 0 (immediate, same-year posttest) / ~1 yr / multi-year (2+). Goes beyond the already-coded binary immediate/delayed: it captures the magnitude of the gap, including very long horizons.
suggestions.rationale: Bleses is the extreme case - the SPELL preschool intervention is measured on a Grade-2 national reading test 3-6 years later, and every long-term effect is null, while the immediate post-tests had been positive; all other studies in this batch measure at end of treatment and several are significant. Effects of early PD may wash out (or, rarely, sleeper-emerge) over years, so a long measurement lag could systematically depress observed g independent of PD quality. The lag length is almost always stated.

suggestions.definition: Whether the PD's theory of action centers on building structured collaboration between adults around the same students (e.g., ESL-and-classroom-teacher co-planning/co-teaching frameworks, whole-school teaching teams), vs PD that targets each teacher's individual practice in isolation. Levels: collaboration/co-teaching central / individual-teacher focus. Distinct from the student-level 'cooperation' learning principle already coded (that is about pupils cooperating, not teachers).
suggestions.rationale: Babinski's entire DCCS program is a teacher-collaboration-and-consultation framework designed to close the 'implementation gap' between ESL and classroom teachers, and Borman's SFA organizes the whole school into coordinated teaching teams with a facilitator; by contrast Allen and Ansari coach individual teachers. Collaboration can sustain practice change between PD sessions and align instruction across the adults a child sees, plausibly moderating transfer to achievement.

suggestions.moderator: Standalone teacher PD vs PD bundled in a comprehensive/multi-component reform
suggestions.definition: Whether the tested intervention is teacher PD as such, or PD packaged inside a larger multi-component program that also adds non-PD elements (new curriculum/materials, one-to-one student tutoring, family-support services, a full-time on-site facilitator). Levels: standalone PD / PD + curriculum / comprehensive whole-school reform (PD + tutoring + family/structural supports). Goes beyond the already-coded 'curriculum-coupled' flag by capturing additional student-facing and structural components.
suggestions.rationale: Borman's Success for All bundles PD with one-to-one tutoring, family-support teams, and a full-time facilitator and yields significant reading effects (g 0.21-0.36); Bierman/Bleses bundle PD with a manualized curriculum; Allen/Ansari are near-pure coaching. When non-PD components (especially direct student tutoring) ride along, attributing the effect to 'teacher PD' overstates PD's lever, and bundling could explain larger effects. This decomposition is reportable from the intervention description.

suggestions.definition: Whether the study itself randomizes more than one intensity/version of the same PD against a common control, giving an internal dose-response contrast (e.g., base program vs base + extended PD/coaching). Levels: single TPD arm / multiple TPD-intensity arms. A study-design feature that flags where dose effects can be estimated within rather than only across studies.
suggestions.rationale: Bleses randomizes SPELL vs SPELL+PD (the latter adds 14 hours of extended professional development/coaching) vs BAU, and the SPELL+PD arm shows the larger - though still ns - reading coefficients (g~0.08-0.10 vs ~-0.02 to -0.07 for base SPELL). Multi-arm studies provide cleaner, confound-free evidence on whether more PD helps; coding their presence lets the meta-analysis weight or sensitivity-check the cross-study dose findings against internal contrasts.

suggestions.moderator: Outcome-measure breadth (narrow targeted skill battery vs broad omnibus achievement test)
suggestions.definition: How closely the outcome instrument's content is scoped to what the PD targets vs a broad standardized achievement test, independent of proximal/distal alignment. Levels: narrow targeted battery (e.g., a specific language/literacy subtest battery) / broad omnibus state or norm-referenced achievement test. Distinct from the already-coded proximal/distal alignment: alignment is about content match to the intervention; breadth is about how diffuse the construct the test samples is.
suggestions.rationale: Babinski explicitly invokes the Hill et al. (2008) benchmark that a 'narrow-focus' measure should be judged against g~0.23 (and its significant effects sit right at that value), whereas Allen and Borman use broad state/normed achievement tests where the same nominal g means something different. Expected effect size scales with measure breadth, so pooling narrow batteries with broad omnibus tests without accounting for breadth can distort heterogeneity; breadth is readable from the instrument description.
